# authorization

## Classes

### Requirement

One route's declared requirement: an opaque, frozen value only this module
mints. Its label and decision live in private fields that only this module
reads, so a copy, a look-alike, an overridden method or a relabelled field
changes nothing a route serves, and registering a non-minted value throws.

### Routes

A declared route table: a frozen, opaque value only [routes](#routes-1) builds.
Its routes live in a private record; including or serving reads only that
record, never a method a copy could override. A table cannot serve itself: only
[serveHost](#servehost), [serveDoors](#servedoors) and
[serveCapability](#servecapability) do, each with the principal its composition
root admits. There is no `use`: a path-wide middleware could serve a path no
route declares.

#### Type Parameters

| Type Parameter      |
| ------------------- |
| `E` _extends_ `Env` |

## Functions

### keyAppAccess()

```ts
function keyAppAccess(
  key,
  installationId,
): {
  level: "read" | "write";
  revision: string;
  grantedBy: string;
} | null;
```

One live key's access to one installation: `write` when its grants admit
`apps.use` there, `read` when they admit `apps.read`, otherwise `null` --
including for an installation added after the key was issued, unless the key
holds "All Apps" (`targets: {kind: "all"}`). The same shape as an Agent's stored
[AppToolPolicy](apps.md#apptoolpolicy); its caller adds `bindingName` (which
varies by caller: the plain installation id for the gate, the uppercased binding
name for MCP) to reach the full `AppToolAccess`.

#### Parameters

| Parameter        | Type                                     |
| ---------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| `key`            | [`LiveOysterKey`](keys.md#liveoysterkey) |
| `installationId` | `string`                                 |

#### Returns

\| \{ `level`: `"read"` \| `"write"`; `revision`: `string`; `grantedBy`:
`string`; \} \| `null`

function serveCapability(table, ports): ServedTable<CapabilityEnv>;

Serve one capability's declared table under the host dispatcher's admission,
read from `c.env`: the App already holds the capability, and each route still
decides its own resource. Every request here is App-mediated, however it was
admitted (a header or a browser socket's query), so `owner("direct")` always
refuses inside a capability.

#### Parameters

| Parameter | Type                                                            |
| --------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `table`   | [`Routes`](#routes)\<[`CapabilityEnv`](host.md#capabilityenv)\> |
| `ports`   | [`AuthorityPorts`](#authorityports)                             |

#### Returns

[`ServedTable`](#servedtable)\<[`CapabilityEnv`](host.md#capabilityenv)\>
